writtenTo: The people of Israel, especially the priests
importantNotes: The sacrificial system points forward to Christ's ultimate sacrifice on the cross.
Leviticus 17:11 — 'the life of a creature is in the blood' — foundational to understanding atonement.
'Be holy, for I am holy' (Lev 19:2) is quoted by Peter in 1 Peter 1:16.
The Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur, chapter 16) is the most sacred day in Israel's calendar.
The book's key word is 'holy' — it appears over 90 times.

chapters.1: Laws for burnt offerings — complete consecration to God.
chapters.2: Laws for grain offerings — thanksgiving and dedication.
chapters.3: Laws for peace offerings — fellowship and communion with God.
chapters.4: Laws for sin offerings — atonement for unintentional sins.
chapters.5: Laws for guilt offerings — restitution for specific trespasses.
chapters.6: Further instructions for burnt, grain, and sin offerings for the priests.
chapters.7: Further instructions for guilt and fellowship offerings; the fat and blood prohibition.
chapters.8: The ordination and consecration of Aaron and his sons as priests.
chapters.9: Aaron offers the first sacrifices; the glory of the LORD appears to all the people.
chapters.10: Nadab and Abihu offer unauthorized fire and are consumed; regulations for priests.
chapters.11: Clean and unclean animals — dietary laws for Israel.
chapters.13: Laws for diagnosing skin diseases (leprosy) and contaminated fabrics.
chapters.14: Rituals for the cleansing of skin diseases and contaminated houses.
chapters.15: Laws concerning bodily discharges and ceremonial uncleanness.
chapters.16: The Day of Atonement — the scapegoat and the annual cleansing of sins.
chapters.17: The centrality of blood sacrifice; prohibition against eating blood.
chapters.18: Laws against sexual immorality and forbidden relationships.
chapters.19: Practical holiness — love your neighbor as yourself; various moral and social laws.
chapters.20: Penalties for serious sins including idolatry and sexual immorality.
chapters.21: Holiness standards for priests; restrictions on priestly conduct.
chapters.22: Regulations for acceptable sacrifices; offerings must be without defect.
chapters.23: The seven appointed feasts of the LORD — Sabbath, Passover, Pentecost, Trumpets, Atonement, Tabernacles.
chapters.24: The lampstand and showbread; blasphemy and the law of retaliation.
chapters.25: The Sabbath Year and the Year of Jubilee — rest for the land and freedom for slaves.
chapters.26: Blessings for obedience and curses for disobedience; God's covenant faithfulness.
chapters.27: Laws about vows, dedications, and tithes.
